Hi Lina — great to meet earlier, and thanks for the sample.

Short answer: we can support both approaches; recommended default is a portal/API push (XML) plus an automated email copy containing the PDF and a small XML attachment for ACK. That gives you machine-readable ingestion plus an archival PDF.

Notes / constraints from our side:
- Our platform can emit a UBL/Invoice XML (we use a slightly opinionated schema). I attached the schema we usually send (invoice_schema_v1.xml).
- VAT tagging: we can include line-level VAT and a total VAT block. For reverse-charge, we can populate the invoice with the proper VAT code and include a tax-evidence PDF as a separate attachment if needed.
- Delivery options: SFTP push, HTTPS POST to your invoice endpoint, or portal batch export. Email PDF with XML companion is a fallback (works but is slower for automated posting).

Proposed next steps:
1) Kimberly to validate that Acme's AP accepts our invoice_schema_v1.xml over SFTP/API and note any field mismatches.
2) Marissa to confirm whether legal needs signed invoices / DocuSign for your region.
3) Lina to confirm preferred delivery channel (SFTP/API/portal + email copy) and go-live date (you mentioned Nov 1).

Kimberly / Marissa — can you own 1/2?

Best,

On Mon, Oct 18, 2026 at 17:02, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Our platform can emit a UBL/Invoice XML (we use a slightly opinionated schema). I attached the schema we usually send (invoice_schema_v1.xml).

Lina / Acme AP — quick ops note from our implementation playbook:
- Most enterprise AP systems accept either: (A) Peppol/UBL via SFTP or HTTPS POST, or (B) XML (custom) via SFTP. Email PDF is commonly accepted but usually requires manual keying unless accompanied by a machine-readable attachment.
- If you want automated ACKs, we can emit an immediate XML-based acknowledgement (ACK) when the invoice is delivered to your endpoint. If using email, we can send a small ACK payload to a dedicated inbox (e.g., invoices-ack@acme.com).
- VAT/reverse-charge: we recommend including a separate tax-evidence PDF (scoped per invoice) and adding the reverse-charge note in the invoice XML in the <TaxNote> field.

Operational recommendation (my preference):
Portal/API push (SFTP or HTTPS) as primary delivery + email copy with PDF + XML companion as fallback for any partners who need it. This minimizes manual processing while keeping archives.

Action items:
- Action: Kimberly to confirm exact XML node names Acme expects for PO matching (we will map ours to yours).
- Action: Marissa to confirm if Acme requires signed/embossed invoices or if a standard PDF with tax evidence is sufficient.

--
Kimberly Park
Billing Integrations Lead
Redwood Inference

Thanks — that plan works for us. A couple of final points from AP before we lock Nov 1: 

- Delivery: use SFTP push to our ingestion endpoint (ap-integration@acme.com / sftp.acme-corp.com) with a daily envelope. Include an email copy to invoices@acme.com for legal/archival.
- Required fields: PO must be present at line 1 and a top-level PO reference. VAT/GST breakdown must be per-line and total. For EU reverse-charge, include the note: "Reverse charge — Article 194" in the tax note.
- Acks: please emit an ACK XML for each invoice delivered; if we cannot process one, return a processing error to the same ACK endpoint so Redwood can retry.
- Reconciliation: can you include a weekly reconciliation CSV with invoice ids and amounts (CSV stub in weekly_artifact.csv)? We will ingest that for matching.

Attached: our PO for initial billing (acme_po_99871.pdf).

If you can confirm SFTP credentials and that the Peppol/UBL or the custom XML will include the fields above, we'll consider Nov 1 confirmed.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Lina
